title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/16/2026
Reason for Admission: Community-acquired pneumonia

Vitals:
Temperature: 101.4 F
Heart Rate: 88 bpm
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min
SpO2: 94% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 12.5 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Chest X-ray: Right lower lobe infiltrates noted.

Review of Systems:
The patient reports productive cough, shortness of breath, and generalized malaise. He denies chest pain, night sweats, or changes in vision. He denies any recent travel or known exposures to sick individuals.

Social History:
The patient lives in a private residence with his wife. He retired five years ago and enjoys gardening and walking. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History:
Father deceased at age 82 due to natural causes. Mother deceased at age 88. No known history of hereditary respiratory conditions in the immediate family.

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 86-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with a three-day history of cough and fever. He was admitted for management of community-acquired pneumonia. During the hospitalization, he was started on a broad-spectrum antibiotic regimen. Microbiology and cultures were obtained upon admission; however, the cultures remained negative and no specific organism was identified. Despite the lack of a specific pathogen, the patient showed a positive clinical response to the antibiotics. His oxygen saturation remained stable on room air. He tolerated his diet well and was able to ambulate in the hallways. He was transitioned to oral medications on the final day of admission.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Community-acquired pneumonia

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 500mg every 8 hours (complete 7-day course)
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever
Multivitamin daily

Follow-up:
The patient should follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a repeat physical examination and a follow-up chest X-ray to ensure resolution of the pneumonia.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/16/2026
explanations: Pneumonia with no organism identified: J18.9 (no HCC).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: A bacterial cause is not documented.
